title: Pubic lice (crabs)
intro: Pubic lice are tiny insects that live in coarse body hair, mostly in the genital area, and cause itching. They are usually passed on through close body contact, including sex. They are not a sign of poor hygiene and are easily treated with medicated lotions or shampoos.

sections.heading: How they spread
paragraphs: Pubic lice crawl from one person to another during close contact and cannot jump or fly. Occasionally they spread through shared bedding, towels or clothing. They need human blood to survive and die within a day or two away from the body. Because they are often passed on during sex, other sexually transmitted infections should be considered.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: The main symptom is itching in the genital area, which tends to be worse at night. You may see small greyish lice or tiny oval eggs, called nits, attached to hair shafts, and small bluish marks or specks of dark blood in underwear. Lice can also affect chest, armpit, beard, eyebrows and eyelashes, but not usually the scalp.

sections.heading: Treatment
paragraphs: Treatment involves insecticide lotions, creams or shampoos containing permethrin or similar agents, available in pharmacies. Apply to all affected hairy areas as directed and wash off after the stated time. Repeat after about a week to kill newly hatched lice. For eyelashes, special treatments from a doctor are needed instead of regular lotions.

sections.heading: Cleaning and contacts
paragraphs: Wash bedding, towels and clothing worn in the last few days at a high temperature, or seal them in a bag for several days. Sexual partners from the last few weeks should be examined and treated at the same time. Avoid close contact until treatment is completed.

sections.heading: Further checks
paragraphs: Because pubic lice can accompany other sexually transmitted infections, a sexual health check is sensible. Seek advice if itching persists after two treatments, or if children are affected, since infestation in children may need further consideration.

examples.title: Treating at home
examples.text: Imagine you find lice in your pubic hair. You could buy a recommended lotion, apply it exactly as directed, wash bedding and repeat treatment after a week.

examples.title: Informing partners
examples.text: Suppose you feel embarrassed to tell your partner. You might explain that pubic lice are common and easily treated, and suggest treating at the same time.
